authentic_trace.mobility_source: authentic FHWA NGSIM US-101 processed trace

training_protocol.initialisation: federated methods: all clients start from the server's single global model; Non_Federated_D3QN: independent random initialisation per client
training_protocol.client_data: each client trains only on its own replay buffer of its own vehicle's transitions (non-IID task mixture, Dirichlet concentration 0.4)
training_protocol.exploration: epsilon-greedy during the first 40% of rounds, greedy afterwards
training_protocol.evaluation: separate environments and seeds, greedy policy of the client's own (post-sync) network, no buffer writes, no gradient steps; parameter hash checked before/after
training_protocol.agent: dueling double DQN, Huber loss, Adam, gamma/learning rate from federated_learning config

limitations: Tasks, channel, queues, rewards and attacks are simulated; only the optional mobility replay is measured data.
Edge queues are deterministic multi-core servers, not M/M/c; tasks of one slot arrive together in a seeded random order.
Attackers are scripted and non-adaptive except the norm-matched stealth sign flip.
Evaluation horizons are short (episodes x steps given in evaluation_config); results do not describe long-run behaviour.
Sweeps use fewer seeds than the main comparison (see sweep_seeds).

provenance_disclosure.task_profiles: 3GPP TR 36.885 derived, scaled by 0.1; modelling assumption
provenance_disclosure.rl_environment: simulated 3GPP-style V2X channel, deterministic edge queues, modelled reward
provenance_disclosure.eval_isolation: independent episodes, separate seeds, greedy policy, no buffer writes, no gradients
provenance_disclosure.participation_rule: clients holding fewer transitions than the minimum training batch (4) could not perform a gradient step; they are non-participants of the round and are not judged. The rule uses the client's available experience, never the ground-truth role. Identical to the live console (web/app.py).
